A.why: She took the other track home, not his path (F7).

B.why: No search along the fence for him; he had moved away (F7).

C.why: F7: at the far fence she saw a narrow track toward a new gate and took that route home.

D.why: Grass covering the edges happened by itself; she planted nothing (F7).

items.source_explanation: F7 says she saw another narrow track toward a new gate and took that route home, so C. A contradicts the new route home; B and D are not in the passage and D misreads the grass growing over the edges.

A.why: F4: shelves held the same books; they only looked empty in dimmer light.

B.why: F4 says the room's contents did not change.

C.why: He moved and later raised the same lamp; no replacement (F4).

items.syllabus_fit: Fair inference item for Class XII.
items.source_explanation: F4 says the shelves held the same books and only looked empty outside the light circle; the statement implies appearance changed, not contents (A). B, C and D contradict or add facts absent from F4.

A.why: Repetition in many sentences is not using few words (F17).

B.why: Unneeded history is not necessary information (F17).

C.why: Gives no useful information, so not necessary and important info (F17).

D.why: Matches F17: only necessary information, few words.

items.source_explanation: F17 defines concise as only necessary, important information in few words, matching D. A, B and C are wordy, irrelevant or empty.

A.why: F3: captains changed the result without replaying the match.

B.why: F3: correcting would turn victory into a tie; captains agreed and changed the result.

C.why: Result became a tie, not an opponent win (F3).

items.source_explanation: F3 states the correction would turn the victory into a tie and the captains agreed and changed the result, so B. A and D contradict F3; C is not supported since a tie is not a loss.

A.why: F5: she sketched one clear bird among the remaining shapes after looking again.

B.why: F5: she returned the next morning to see the wall in the light it was designed for; also after the boy's remark.

C.why: F5: she did not erase the sky.

D.why: F5: she did not declare the boy correct.

items.missing_decisive_condition: Stem asks what she did 'after' the boy's remark; both the sketching and the return next morning follow it, so two options are established.
items.syllabus_fit: Fair literal item but flawed key design.
items.quality_note: Two correct options (A and B); stem does not restrict to the immediate action.
items.source_explanation: F5 supports both A (sketched one clear bird) and B (returned the next morning). C and D are contradicted by 'did not erase the sky or declare the boy correct'. No single answer.

items.missing_decisive_condition: The uncle's city is never given in the passage; an outside fact would be required.
items.quality_note: Asks for a detail absent from the passage; options are arbitrary.
items.source_explanation: F10 says only that the grandmother left to stay with his uncle; no city is mentioned, so none of the options can be established.

A.why: F2: faster speech made words hard to follow.

B.why: F2: her teacher asked the question; the organiser only shortened time.

C.why: F2: teacher asked which idea she most wanted remembered; she then removed the anecdote and examples keeping the central argument.

D.why: F2: she retained the central argument.

items.quality_note: Stem slightly awkward ('Why was Amina able to explain') but answerable.
items.source_explanation: F2 shows she chose cuts by identifying the idea to preserve, retaining the central argument, and so could explain the removal (C). A, B and D contradict F2.

A.why: F9: she wanted it to win but asked for a check so it would not be attached from memory; her reply says entries judged as submitted.

B.why: F9: she said she helped entries be judged as they were submitted.

C.why: F9: not stated that the coordinator asked her to announce early.

D.why: F9: she noticed this before the judges arrived.

items.source_explanation: F9 has Leela state she helped the entries be judged as submitted and she would do the same for anyone (B). A is contrary to that fairness motive; C is unstated; D contradicts 'before the judges arrived'.

A.why: F9-like F8: he realised asking the right person could be useful assistance.

B.why: F8: his initial feeling, which he revised.

D.why: F8: he knew the costumes were needed soon.

items.source_explanation: F8 states Rohan realised that asking the right person could be useful assistance, which A restates. B is his initial view, C contradicts 'thanked both', D contradicts 'needed soon'.
